definition: Recollection means the act or power of remembering, or a specific memory called back to mind.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word recollection. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know recollection should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Grandpa's recollection of the 1964 flood grew sharper as he walked us along the levee where it happened.
An impression is only a vague sense that something happened; a recollection brings back real detail.
A flashback is more intense than a recollection — the past floods back so vividly it feels like reliving it.

Memory is the everyday, all-purpose word for something remembered, or for the power of remembering itself. Recollection is more deliberate and formal — the act of actively calling something back to mind, often under questioning. You simply have memories; a recollection is summoned.

Remembrance is about honoring the past — ceremonies, keepsakes, moments of silence for what deserves to stay in mind. A recollection is just the memory itself, called back to mind for some practical purpose. Remembrance commemorates; a recollection merely reports what the mind retrieves.

A reminiscence is a fond, story-like memory shared aloud — the kind traded over dinner about old summers. A recollection is plainer and cooler: a memory called back to mind, with no warmth implied. Reminiscences entertain a table; recollections answer questions.

Eight months after the derailment, the inquiry finally called the night dispatcher, Marisol Vega, to testify.
The board did not want her opinions; it wanted her recollection of the eleven minutes before the alarm, retrieved as exactly as she could manage.
Counsel walked her through it question by question: which light she checked first, what the radio said, when she stood up from the console.
Vega answered slowly, sometimes closing her eyes to call a detail back before she spoke.
Nothing she said was fond or rehearsed; it was plain retrieval, summoned one question at a time and offered as evidence.
